title: Microsoft Purview DLP: policy sync status within 30 minutes (Worldwide)
summary: The rollout dates, automatic default, device-status path and Graph operation are supported. Licensing should identify the published Endpoint DLP entitlement rather than leave the model unknown; a few supporting sources also need citations.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: The troubleshooting documentation says policy sync status in the devices list can take up to 2 hours to update.
claims.quote: It might take up to 2 hours for the status in the devices list to update.

claims.claim: The Endpoint DLP overview says policy updates generally take about an hour to synchronize across the service.
claims.quote: When a policy is updated in Microsoft Purview portal, it generally takes about an hour for those updates to be synchronized across the service.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the 30-minute DLP sync target at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "30 minutes" "policy" "sync"'; 'Purview Endpoint DLP 30 minute policy sync licensing prerequisites Authorized Groups'. Opened dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync and endpoint-dlp-learn-about; they retain the 2-hour and approximately 1-hour descriptions.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Per-device policy sync status is available in Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Device onboarding > Devices.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery executes an advanced hunting query.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery

claims.claim: The Graph request body specifies the query using the Query property.
claims.quote: In the request body, provide a JSON object with the Query property, and optionally include the Timespan and workspaceId properties.

claims.claim: The DeviceInfo table's DlpInfo column exposes Endpoint DLP policy synchronization information corresponding to the device onboarding page.
claims.quote: The JSON object can be used to query and report on device configuration status, policy synchronization status, Endpoint DLP enablement, and other configuration details for onboarded devices. These values correspond to the device information available in the DLP device onboarding page.

claims.claim: Policy sync status has Updated, Not updated and Not available values.
claims.quote: Field value | Configuration status | Policy sync status ... Updated ... Not updated ... Not available

claims.claim: Policy sync status indicates whether an onboarded device received the latest policy.
claims.quote: If the status is Updated, the device successfully received the latest policy version. ... If the status is Not updated or Not available, follow the remediation steps in the details pane and the steps in the workflow diagram.

claims.claim: Devices must be online to receive policy updates.
claims.quote: Devices must be online for the policy update to happen.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents a 24-hour policy sync requirement for Authorized Groups changes.
claims.quote: For Authorized Groups changes, the policy needs 24 hours to sync.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified whether the 30-minute improvement covers Authorized Groups changes.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Endpoint DLP" "Authorized Groups" "30"'; 'Purview Endpoint DLP 30 minute policy sync licensing prerequisites Authorized Groups'. Read MC1317834, dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync and endpoint-dlp-learn-about; no passage connects the new SLA to Authorized Groups.

claims.claim: A custom account viewing device management settings must have Compliance admin, Compliance data admin, Global reader, Security admin or Global admin.
claims.quote: If you want to use a custom account to view the device management settings, it must be in one of these roles: Compliance admin; Compliance data admin; Global reader; Security admin; Global admin

claims.claim: Device management supports Entra roles, not Purview roles.
claims.quote: Device management currently only supports Entra roles. Purview roles are not supported.

claims.claim: The status surface reports whether a device received the latest policy rather than configuring enforcement speed.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device.

claims.claim: The documented interactive advanced hunting route uses the Microsoft Defender portal.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft Defender portal ... Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting ... Query the DeviceInfo table ... Expand the DlpInfo column

claims.claim: The Graph hunting query requires the permissions listed in its API reference.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | ThreatHunting.Read.All | ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All ... Application | ThreatHunting.Read.All | ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP policy changes can be tested in simulation or audit-only mode before enforcement.
claims.quote: When you deploy a new policy or need to modify an existing one, you should run it in simulation mode, and then review the alerts to assess its accuracy.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-test-dlp-policies to sources for the recommendation to test policy changes in simulation mode.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends optionally informing security and compliance teams about faster policy changes.
claims.quote: Optionally, inform security and compliance teams that DLP changes will take effect more quickly to support faster response expectations.
